R133.tradeoff: FIXTURE: a user with many habits misses some pushes (they stay in-app).
R133.why: FIXTURE: more than three pushes a day reads as spam and gets the app's notifications turned off.

R29.tradeoff: FIXTURE: a sync burst can hit 429 and must retry after the window.
R29.why: FIXTURE: one signed-in client must not starve the API for everyone else.

R56.tradeoff: FIXTURE: heavy users must archive habits to add more.
R56.why: FIXTURE: the home screen returns every active habit in one unpaginated response, so the count is capped.

R63.tradeoff: FIXTURE: a user who wants another period must create a new habit.
R63.why: FIXTURE: a habit's period is fixed so that its history and its habit_targets rows never mix weeks, months and years.

R75.tradeoff: FIXTURE: a user returning after two months cannot back-fill.
R75.why: FIXTURE: check-ins older than 60 days would rewrite long-closed history periods.

R20.why: FIXTURE PROPOSAL: reuse of a rotated refresh token signals a stolen token.

R26.why: FIXTURE PROPOSAL: account deletion is hard so that erasure requests are met.

questions.text: Why can't the period of a habit be changed after it is created?
Why is a user limited to 50 active habits?
Why are check-ins dated more than 60 days ago refused?
Why is a signed-in user limited to 120 requests per minute?
Why does a user get at most 3 pushes per local day?
Why is deleting an account a hard delete?
Why does reusing a rotated refresh token revoke the whole session?
Why is the email stored lower-cased at registration?
Why does deleting a habit keep its rows in the database?
Why do quiet hours suppress a nudge's push?
Why does dismissing a nudge apply to every device of the user?
What does "active window" mean in this spec?
What does "daily pass" mean in this spec?

R70.anchor_text: DELETE /v1/habits/{id} answers 204 and removes the habit.
R70.why: FIXTURE: soft deletes let the user's other devices sync tombstones.

R8.anchor_text: The email is stored as given.
R8.why: FIXTURE: emails are compared case-insensitively everywhere.
